updates.name: Margaret S. Torn
updates.bio: Ecologist and biogeochemist who co-leads Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory's Climate and Carbon Sciences Program and holds an adjunct professorship in UC Berkeley's Energy and Resources Group. She studies terrestrial carbon and nutrient cycling, soil carbon storage and soil-atmosphere greenhouse-gas exchange using field experiments, 14C/13C isotopes and models.
updates.research_interests: soil carbon cycling and storage (controls by soil minerals, nutrient status, climate and land use); carbon and nutrient cycling in terrestrial ecosystems; soil-atmosphere trace-gas flux; radiocarbon and stable-isotope (14C, 13C) analysis; land-use effects incl. bioenergy crops and carbon sequestration management; climate-change impacts on ecosystems; ecosystem-climate feedbacks
updates.current_title: Co-head, Climate and Carbon Sciences Program (LBNL); Adjunct Professor, Energy and Resources Group (UC Berkeley)

Her publications centre on wildlife habitat in managed northern hardwood and white pine forests of New England, including long-term bird, small-mammal and salamander responses to silviculture and decades of forest research at the Bartlett Experimental Forest.

updates.name: Mark A. Liebig
updates.bio: Research soil scientist with USDA-ARS at the Northern Great Plains Research Laboratory in Mandan, North Dakota, since 1999, and adjunct faculty in soil science at North Dakota State University. He quantifies how cropping, grazing and fire management affect soil properties in Great Plains agroecosystems and builds evaluation tools for producers and conservationists.
updates.research_interests: conservation management effects on soil properties and processes in rainfed cropping systems; soil property dynamics under grazing and fire management; Visual Soil Assessment in semiarid agroecosystems; Northern Plains LTAR Cropland Common Experiment (prevailing vs aspirational treatments)

updates.name: Mark C. Serreze
updates.bio: Arctic climate scientist who directs the National Snow and Ice Data Center within CIRES and is a Distinguished Professor of Geography at the University of Colorado Boulder (PhD, CU 1989). He studies Arctic change - sea-ice loss, warming and permafrost thaw - and currently leads the NSF Navigating the New Arctic Arctic Rain on Snow Study (AROSS).
updates.research_interests: Arctic climate change; sea-ice decline; Arctic warming and permafrost thaw; rain-on-snow and melt-refreeze events and their ecological and societal impacts (Arctic Rain on Snow Study, AROSS); science outreach

Earlier he was a USGS Southwest Biological Science Center research ecologist at the Canyonlands and Colorado Plateau research stations, headed resource stewardship for NPS's Southeast Utah Group, and served with BLM's North Slope Science Initiative and at Wrangell-St. Elias.

updates.name: Mark E. Mort
updates.bio: Professor of ecology and evolutionary biology at the University of Kansas and a Chancellors Club Teaching Professor. A plant systematist, he uses chloroplast and nuclear DNA sequences to reconstruct angiosperm relationships, especially in Crassulaceae and Asteraceae, and studies island plant evolution, notably Aeonium in the Canary Islands and Tolpis in Macaronesia.
updates.research_interests: angiosperm phylogenetics; Crassulaceae (incl. Crassula, Aeonium) and Asteraceae (Tolpis) systematics; island evolution (Canary Islands, Macaronesia); physiological evolution; systematic methods; biogeography
updates.current_affiliation: University of Kansas, Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology

updates.name: Mark H. Sherfy
updates.bio: Deputy Center Director of USGS's Northern Prairie Wildlife Research Center, based in Jamestown, North Dakota. His expertise is threatened and endangered species, especially interior least terns and piping plovers, with work on nest-monitoring methods and on piping plover breeding habitat, dispersal and survival across the northern Great Plains.
